lpn_area_hint_window_start.on: Click one corner of the window.

lpn_confirm_labels_restore.on: Set the label columns back to their original values? This resets which properties are shown, the text before and after each one, the decimals, and the drop order. Your drawing and your other settings are not changed.

lpn_coord_off_world.on: That is off the map. Pseudo Mercator latitude ranges from -85.05 to 85.05 and longitude ranges from -180 to 180.

lpn_cp_add_tip.on: Adds a row to the design table and opens it for editing.

lpn_cp_applies_tip.on: Applies to: Comma separated list of ID prefixes for assets that use this property, such as J,L,R.

lpn_cp_bad_case.on: This value is not ALL CAPS as required for this property.

lpn_cp_bad_chars.on: This value uses a character this property does not allow.

lpn_cp_bad_high.on: This value is above the high limit of this property.

lpn_cp_bad_integer.on: This value is not a whole number as required for this property.

lpn_cp_bad_length.on: This value is longer than this property allows.

lpn_cp_bad_low.on: This value is below the low limit of this property.

lpn_cp_bad_minlength.on: This value is shorter than this property allows.

lpn_cp_bad_number.on: This value is not a number as required for this property.

lpn_cp_bad_space.on: White space is allowed only between other characters.

lpn_cp_design_tip.on: One row per custom property, and each opens to show: Key, Label, Applies to, Validate as, Allow or restrict, the characters field named by that choice, Length lower limit, Length upper limit, Low limit, High limit.

lpn_cp_edit_tip.on: Opens the design of this custom property, where every part of it is shown at full length.

lpn_cp_flag.on: {label}: {reason} The value is kept exactly as you typed it.

lpn_cp_high_tip.on: High limit: This is the largest value you expect. Numbers are compared as numbers and text in dictionary order.

lpn_cp_key_needed.on: Give this custom property a key with no spaces.

lpn_cp_key_taken.on: Another custom property already uses that key.

lpn_cp_key_tip.on: Key: A property is stored under this name. Spaces are not allowed, and a prefix is added for you so that your key can never collide with a built-in field.

lpn_cp_label_tip.on: Label: A reader sees this on the properties box, in Find and at the head of a table column.

lpn_cp_length_tip.on: Length upper limit: Any longer entry is flagged.

lpn_cp_low_tip.on: Low limit: This is the smallest value you expect. Numbers are compared as numbers and text in dictionary order.

lpn_cp_minlength_tip.on: Length lower limit: Any shorter entry is flagged, which is how you find the empty and the half-typed entries.

lpn_cp_none.on: No custom property is designed yet.

lpn_cp_remove_tip.on: Removes this property from the design table. Values already typed on your assets are kept in the file and come back if you design the same key again.

lpn_cp_restrict_mode_tip.on: Allow or restrict: The given characters are either the only ones a value may use or the ones it may not use.

lpn_cp_restrict_tip.on: Restrict these characters: A value may use only the characters listed here, or none of them, where "@" means any letter; "#" means any numeric digit, and you must separately list "-", ".", and "," if they are allowed; and any white space characters must be between other characters.

lpn_cp_validate_tip.on: Validate as: This says what a good value looks like. The case rules read the English alphabet only, which is a stated limit. Choose Do not validate to accept anything.

lpn_crs_list_tip.on: The projections left by the two filters above. Choose one and press Select.

lpn_crs_name_tip.on: Shows only the projections whose name or EPSG code contains what you type. Try a zone number, or UTM, or Mercator.

lpn_crs_noview.on: No place has been searched for yet, so the whole list is offered. Search for a place above or zoom the map to narrow it.
lpn_crs_noview.answer: Edited, and confirm that this describes the specified and targeted behavior, that the visible map area is used to filter the list.

lpn_crs_place.answer: OK. And this seems like a duplicate string maybe.

lpn_crs_place_projected.on: A projected project opens on its own plane, not at the place you searched for. Putting that plane on the Earth needs a coordinate transform, which this page does not have yet.
lpn_crs_place_projected.answer: This is a problem. The projected project needs to open at the place you searched for. We know the lat/lon and zoom level they searched for. That needs to be the initial view of their project.

lpn_crs_place_tip.on: Type a town, an address, or a landmark, and the map view moves there. The words you type go to OpenStreetMap’s place-name service, which asks your permission the first time. A new geographic project also starts at the place you find here.
lpn_crs_place_tip.answer: OK. And this seems like a duplicate string maybe.

lpn_crs_unplaceable.on: This page has no transform for that projection, so a project on it opens on its own plane: no map behind the drawing, no arrival at the place you searched for, and no elevations from the land surface. Your coordinates are unaffected. Another projection covering the same area will have all three.

lpn_crs_unplaceable_mark.answer: Please explain to me what this is in response to. What's the case for this label?

lpn_crs_view_tip.on: Offers only the projections that cover the place the map is looking at. Turn it off to read the whole list.

lpn_curve_library_link_tip.on: Opens the Libraries box on its Curves section, where a curve is added, described, edited and deleted. An asset states which curve it uses.

lpn_curve_long_note.on: Curve ID {name} has {count} points; it is shown here and edited under Libraries, Curves.

lpn_curve_shared_note.on: These points belong to curve ID {name}, which {ids} also use. Changing them here changes them there too.

lpn_customer_detached.on: ⚠ This customer is not connected to a pipe, so its demand is not in the answers. Delete it, or draw a pipe and move the customer onto it.

lpn_customer_detached_count.on: {n} customers are not connected to a pipe. Their demand is not accounted for.

lpn_customer_fixed_head.on: ⚠ The near end of that pipe holds a fixed water surface, so this demand does not affect the simulation.

lpn_demand_add_tip.on: Add another demand at this junction, with its own base demand, pattern and description. The demands add up.

lpn_diag_not_converged_drawn.on: The solve did not converge. These numbers are the last iteration, not an answer. Do not use them.

lpn_diag_not_converged_error.on: It stopped after {iterations} iterations at a relative error of {error}, against an accuracy of {accuracy}.

lpn_elev_dem_none.on: The DEM gave no height for this node.

lpn_elev_dem_sample_tip.on: Reads the elevation of the DEM at this node and shows it below for review before changing the current entry. The horizontal DEM resolution is about 30 m for most of the Earth, and finer where better data exists.

lpn_elev_dem_use_tip.on: Puts the elevation of the DEM at this node into the Elevation box above, replacing what is there. It reads the DEM first if it has not been read yet. One Undo puts it back.

lpn_energy_col_avg_kw_tip.on: The average power used when this pump was running. It is not averaged over idle periods, so a pump that was idle for much of the extended period simulation still reports the power it used while it ran.

lpn_energy_currency_tip.on: Whatever you write here is printed beside every money figure. It is a label. Prices and costs are never converted, so write the prices in the currency you have written here.

lpn_energy_curve_note.on: These pumps call an efficiency curve with no points: {ids}. They ran at the efficiency set for the whole network.
lpn_energy_curve_note.answer: OK. But isn't this impossible? Doesn't the software reject such a curve?
lpn_energy_curve_note.reply: Not impossible, and it is reachable two ways. (1) An imported .inp whose [ENERGY] row names an efficiency curve that no [CURVES] section defines: we never reject a file, we take the supported subset and report every difference, so the pump keeps the reference and falls back to the global efficiency. (2) The Library's own Add a curve button, which deliberately mints a pump head curve with NO points -- invented points would be head nobody typed. js/looped-network.js:31586 fires on both, and the sibling string lpn_pump_effic_unstated covers case (1) on the pump's own popup.

lpn_energy_demand_charge_tip.on: What the utility charges per kW for the peak load demanded by the pumps in the system.

lpn_energy_efficiency_tip.on: The wire-to-water efficiency used for every pump that does not carry an efficiency curve of its own. EPANET uses 75 percent when nothing is stated.

lpn_energy_menu_tip.on: What share of the run each pump was on, what power it drew and what it cost over the last extended period simulation.

lpn_energy_needs_run.on: Pump energy is power integrated over the run, so it needs an extended period simulation: the EPANET engine and a total run time. Set a Total run time in Settings, Calculation, Time, press the Calculate button, then open Water, Reports, Pump energy.

lpn_energy_no_price.on: No price of power is stated, so every cost here is zero. Set one under Settings, Energy.

lpn_energy_no_pumps.on: This network has no pumps, so there is nothing drawing power.

lpn_energy_price_note.on: This page offers no price of its own. What power costs depends on the utility, the country, the hour and the year, so a number supplied here would be read as a recommendation. Enter the price from your own tariff.

lpn_energy_price_pattern_tip.on: A pattern that multiplies the price at each pattern step, which is how an off-peak rate is specified. Leave it empty for one price throughout the run.

lpn_energy_price_tip.on: What one kilowatt hour costs. It applies to every pump that does not carry a price of its own. Leave it empty and every cost in the report is zero.

lpn_energy_price_zero.on: This network states a price of zero, so every cost here is zero. Change it under Settings, Energy.

lpn_energy_pump_price_tip.on: What one kilowatt hour costs at this pump. Leave it empty and the pump pays the price set for the whole network under Settings, Energy.

lpn_engine_needed_failed.on: The EPANET solver has not yet been loaded, cannot be loaded, and this network can only be solved by it. It will be loaded when you are connected to the internet.
lpn_engine_needed_failed.answer: There is that "and" construction again that is not best for an engineering software. I edited it.

lpn_engine_needed_loading.on: Loading EPANET solver while you build. Results will be available when completely loaded.
lpn_engine_needed_loading.answer: Tom's own sentence, written by him in the instruction that commissioned the feature: "we show a banner 'Loading EPANET solver while you build. Results will be available when completely loaded.' while it fetches". Recorded because the words are his, not because anybody approved ours.

lpn_engine_wait.on: Loading solver. Results delayed momentarily. Continue working.

lpn_engine_wait_bytes.on: Solver {kb} KB loaded so far. The total is not available, so the percentage of completion is unknown.

lpn_ff_accounting.on: Fire flow is drawn at the junction itself. That is the method used here, and it is the usual one. The hydrant, its lateral, and its nozzle are not modelled, so a real hydrant delivers less than the flow shown here.

lpn_ff_col_static_tip.on: The pressure at this junction before any fire flow is drawn, with the system's ordinary demands still running. Nothing is shut off to measure it, so this is not a zero-flow pressure for the system; it is the same pressure the map shows at this junction. AWWA M31 and NFPA 291 both call this reading the static pressure, and it is where a fire flow test starts.

lpn_ff_design_all.on: Every other junction and every pipe

lpn_ff_design_none.on: Nothing in the chosen set was drawn down by any junction tested.

lpn_ff_design_off_note.on: The effect on the rest of the system was not checked in this run.

lpn_ff_design_tip.on: A separate question from whether the junction can deliver the flow: with that flow drawn there, does anything else fall below its minimum pressure or run too fast? Choosing to check it costs no extra calculation.

lpn_ff_engine_cost.on: Available fire flow is a search, so the whole network is solved about sixteen times for every junction tested. A large system takes minutes. You can stop it at any time and keep what it has already worked out.

lpn_ff_engine_epanet.on: This is worked out with the EPANET engine.

lpn_ff_engine_native.on: This is worked out with the built-in solver.

lpn_ff_err_at_rest.on: Already below the residual with nothing drawn

lpn_ff_err_solve.on: The solver reported an error and gave no answer.

lpn_ff_err_unknown.on: No answer, and the reason given is {id}

lpn_ff_intro.on: Each junction in turn is asked to draw a fire flow on top of the demand it already has. Nothing in your project is changed; the whole run is made on a copy.

lpn_ff_iso.on: ISO credits a single hydrant with at most {flow}. That credit limit has not been applied here because we do not know how many hydrants a node may represent.

lpn_ff_maxvelocity_tip.on: A pipe running above this while a fire flow is drawn is reported as a design issue.

lpn_ff_menu_tip.on: Test every junction: how much can it deliver while it still holds its residual pressure, and does drawing the required flow there create unacceptable drawdown anywhere else?

lpn_ff_minpressure_tip.on: A junction that falls below this while another one is drawing its fire flow is reported as a design issue.

lpn_ff_no_junctions.on: This project has no junctions yet, so there is nothing to test.

lpn_ff_no_selection.on: No junction is selected. Choose one on the map, or test every junction.

lpn_ff_required_tip.on: The flow required by your code or your fire authority at a hydrant. One junction at a time is tested against this same number.

lpn_ff_residual_tip.on: 20 psi is the AWWA M31 and NFPA 291 convention for available fire flow.

lpn_ff_scope_tip.on: Choose the set before you run. Testing every junction in a large system can take minutes.

lpn_ff_stale.on: The drawing changed, so the fire flow results were cleared. Run it again.

lpn_ff_steady.on: Only the current time step is tested. Fire flow is normally added to maximum day demand.

lpn_ff_stopped.on: Stopped after {done} of {total} junctions. What is below is what had already been worked out.

lpn_ff_summary.on: {clean} with nothing wrong. {fire} failed the fire flow. {design} affected the rest of the system.

lpn_field_account_tip.on: Whatever your own records call this service. It is a name on a demand and nothing here looks anything up by it, so it can be an account number, a street address, or a note to yourself. It stays in your project file.

lpn_field_coord_tip.on: Type a coordinate location to place this node exactly. In a scenario this location applies in that scenario alone, just as dragging it does; in Base it places the node everywhere.

lpn_field_demand_category_tip.on: Name or description of the category.

lpn_field_desc_tip.on: For your own use, such as a street corner or what a pipe is made of. It is carried into and out of the EPANET file, where it sits at the end of the part's own row. No calculation reads it. A line break becomes a space, because the file has nowhere to put one.

lpn_field_emitter_tip.on: An extra outflow that depends on pressure, for a sprinkler, an open outlet, or a modeled leak. The flow it releases is this coefficient times the pressure raised to the emitter exponent, which is set once for the whole network under Settings, Calculation, Hydraulics. Leave it blank on an ordinary junction.

lpn_field_fittings_tip.on: A list of fittings from the project library. Its quantities and coefficients are added up into this pipe’s minor loss coefficient, and the coefficient box is then read only. Leave this unselected to type the coefficient yourself.

lpn_field_meter_count_tip.on: How many identical services this one customer stands for, so that forty-two single-family connections along one main can be one symbol in one place. The total below is the demand above times this count.

lpn_field_meter_demand_tip.on: What each service at this customer requires. Find and replace can leverage the distinction between blank and 0.
lpn_field_meter_demand_tip.answer: Edited. You make the pedantic point in multiple locations that blank is not the same as zero, but this is not a helpful thing to say; it's a truth without information. Instead, say what blank would be used for. I am making an attempt, but I want you to edit my wording if I misunderstood. Please make this a general point learned once we achieve mutual understanding about this.

lpn_field_meter_lumped_tip.on: Nearest node; this customer's demands are added there.

lpn_field_meter_offset_tip.on: Positive is to the right of the pipe looking from its first node toward its second. Typing a value here can move the customer to the other side of the main, and it always squares the service line to the main.

lpn_field_meter_pattern_tip.on: How this customer’s demand rises and falls through the run. It multiplies the total demand, so it acts on every service this customer stands for. Leave it at No pattern to follow the project’s Default demand pattern.
lpn_field_meter_pattern_tip.answer: Edited. Note that I removed your habitual "and it" construction where you mean "If this, then that."

lpn_field_meter_pipe.answer: Edited. We want to allow connecting directly to a node.

lpn_field_meter_pipe_suggest.on: The nearest asset is {id}. Type it here to serve this customer from it.

lpn_field_meter_pipe_tip.on: The asset that this service connects to. Type another one here or in the Customers table to change it, or drag the connection point to a different asset.
lpn_field_meter_pipe_tip.answer: This is stale. Connection point can no longer be dragged. Edited. Check.

lpn_field_meter_station.answer: OK. We need to rule on whether we allow non-perpendicular connections.

lpn_field_meter_station_tip.on: How far along the pipe the service connects, as a percentage of the pipe from its first node to its second. 0 is at one end and 100 is at the other. The circle on the pipe does the same thing with the pointer.
lpn_field_meter_station_tip.answer: We need to rule on whether we allow non-perpendicular connections.

lpn_field_meter_total_tip.on: The demand per service times the number of services. This is the number added to the junction named below.

lpn_field_pipetype_tip.on: The pipe type in the project library that this pipe uses. Properties included in the pipe type are disabled for editing here. Detach the pipe type to enable editing here.

lpn_field_tag_tip.on: A tag can have any meaning you require, such as a pressure zone or a work order. No calculation here or in EPANET reads it. A tag is one word: EPANET stops reading at the first space, so a space is refused as you type it. It is carried into and out of the EPANET file.

lpn_field_text_all_zoom.answer: Default needs to be off. I see that you turned it on by default, and that already has caused me grief. Only a few texts would be privileged to have this on. Otherwise ok.

lpn_field_text_all_zoom_tip.on: Keep this text on the drawing however far out you zoom. Untick it and the text hides with the other labels once the view is wider than the labeling threshold set under Map and page.
lpn_field_text_all_zoom_tip.answer: Default needs to be off. I see that you turned it on by default, and that already has caused me grief. Only a few texts would be privileged to have this on. Otherwise ok.

lpn_field_text_attached_tip.on: This text was placed close enough to an asset to follow it, so it moves with that asset and has a leader. A text on a leader takes its horizontal and vertical alignment from the side it sits on, which is why those two rows are not offered while it is attached.

lpn_file_import_survey_tip.on: Read a list of surveyed points from a text file and make one junction at each point, taking the new-asset settings for everything the file does not state. No pipes are drawn, and no row is ever dropped without being named. It reads the coordinate system this project already uses, georeferenced or not.

lpn_find_conn_no_fixed.on: This network has no reservoir or tank, so it has no source to reach. Only "no links" and "no open links" can be searched.

lpn_find_conn_nolinksource.on: No link path to a source

lpn_find_conn_noopensource.on: No open path to a source

lpn_find_filter_tip.on: Show only the parts that match this query in one of the tables below the map. The drawing is not changed and nothing is deleted.

lpn_find_op_conn_nolinksource.on: no link path to a source

lpn_find_op_conn_noopensource.on: no open path to a source

lpn_find_q_aside.on: These controls cannot write the query below, so they are hidden.

lpn_find_q_err_close.on: This bracket ( was opened and never closed.

lpn_find_q_err_dot.on: Put a dot between what to search and its property, like Junction.ID

lpn_find_q_err_empty.on: The query is empty, so nothing will be searched.

lpn_find_q_err_end.on: Nothing was expected after this. Join two searches with {and} or {or}.

lpn_find_q_err_op.on: Not a condition for {prop}: {w}. Try one of: {list}

lpn_find_q_err_prop.on: Not a property of {scope}: {w}. Try one of: {list}

lpn_find_q_err_quote.on: Put quotes around a text value: {w} is not a number.

lpn_find_q_err_quote_end.on: This quoted text has no closing quote.

lpn_find_q_err_scope.on: Not something to search: {w}. Try one of: {list}

lpn_find_q_err_value.on: This condition needs a value after it: {op}

lpn_find_query_tip.on: The same search, written as one line. Change the controls and it rewrites itself, or type in it and the controls follow.

lpn_georef_backdrop_unrotated.on: The background image was moved and resized with the model, but it could not be rotated. Use Background image > Move to line it up.

lpn_georef_projected.on: This project already states a map projection, so its coordinates cannot be placed on the map a second time.

lpn_georef_save_locked.on: Finish the placement with the "Keep this placement" button, or press Cancel, before you save. The project is still being placed, so what is on the screen is not yet what would be written to the file.

lpn_georef_tab_locked.on: Finish the placement with the "Keep this placement" button, or press Cancel, before you switch projects. The placement belongs to this project and cannot follow you to another one.

lpn_georef_twopt_done.on: The model now sits on the two points you gave. Check it, then press Keep this placement.

lpn_georef_twopt_pick1.on: Click a point on your drawing whose latitude and longitude you know.

lpn_georef_twopt_pick2.on: Now click a second known point, as far from the first one as you can.

lpn_georef_twopt_same.on: That is the point you picked first. Pick a different one.

lpn_georef_twopt_tip.on: Place the model exactly, when you already know where two points on your drawing really are. Click one of them, type its latitude and longitude, then do the same for a second point. The place, the size and the turn all follow from those two. Press this button again to stop picking.

lpn_gpv_curve_source_tip.on: The curve in the Libraries box that says how much head this valve loses at each flow. Several valves can use the same curve, and editing it there changes all of them. This valve holds only the reference; the points themselves are read and edited under Libraries, Curves.

lpn_inp_drop_energy.on: This EPANET file includes pumping cost modelling data. This page does not work out energy or cost, so nothing here uses those numbers. They are kept, and they are written back if you save an EPANET file.

lpn_inp_drop_file_options.on: This file refers to an auxiliary file: Map, which holds coordinates, or Hydraulics, which holds hydraulics already worked out. This page cannot open either, so the lines are kept as they are and written back if you save an EPANET file.

lpn_inp_drop_net_options.on: This EPANET .net file states settings that this page has no control for, so their values are listed here rather than carried across. Everything else came over. If you need them, open the file in EPANET and use File, Export, Network to save it as an .inp file, then import that.

lpn_inp_drop_quality_options.on: This file states EPANET water quality options: Quality, which names the kind of water quality analysis, and two settings that go with a chemical, Relative diffusivity and Quality tolerance. Water age and source trace are worked out here; a chemical is not, so those two settings are kept without being used. All of them are written back if you save an EPANET file.

lpn_inp_drop_report.on: This file holds EPANET's own settings for the reports it prints. This page shows its answers in its own way, so nothing here uses them. They are kept, and they are written back if you save an EPANET file.

lpn_inp_drop_rules.on: This file has rule-based controls. They are not applied here, so the pipes, pumps and valves they name stay at the state written in the file. The rules themselves are kept, and they are written back if you save an EPANET file.

lpn_inp_drop_sections.on: This file holds a part that this page does not read at all. Nothing here uses it. It is kept whole, and it is written back if you save an EPANET file.

lpn_inp_drop_sources_mixing.on: This file says where a chemical is dosed into the network, and how the water in a tank mixes. A dose shows up on the node it is added at, and a tank says which mixing model it follows. Both the dose and the mixing model are calculated by the EPANET engine only.

lpn_inp_drop_tags.on: This file gives tags to some of its junctions, pipes or other assets. There is no place on this page to see a tag or change one yet. The tags are kept, and they are written back if you save an EPANET file.

lpn_inp_export_flat_coords.on: An EPANET file holds one position for each node. This scenario places {n} of them somewhere else, and those are the positions in the file. Every other scenario keeps its own positions in your project file alone.
lpn_inp_export_flat_coords.answer: This is unclear. Please proofread and reword.

lpn_inp_export_flat_customers.on: An EPANET file has no customers. The demand of the {n} customers in this project goes into the file as a demand row on the junction each one is added to, and each row is named with the customer’s tag. What the file cannot hold is the customer: where it sits, which pipe serves it, where along that pipe the service connects, and how many services one customer stands for. Your own project file keeps all of that.

lpn_inp_export_flat_fittings.on: An EPANET file cannot hold the list of elbows, valves and tees in your project file. The minor loss coefficient of {n} pipes here is added up from a fittings list. The total goes into the file exactly as it stands, so nothing about the answers changes.

lpn_inp_export_flat_lead.on: The exported EPANET file is numerically equivalent to this project. But it has no place for the following things:

lpn_inp_export_flat_types.on: {n} pipes here refer to {t} pipe types. In the file each of those pipes carries its own copy of the numbers, so the answers are the same. What the file cannot hold is the pipe type itself, so editing one definition and having every pipe follow is something only your own project file records.

lpn_labels_customer_note.on: A customer label shows the values ticked here. It is drawn at the same text size as every other label on the map.

lpn_labels_customer_width.on: Widest view that attempts to display customer labels

lpn_labels_customer_width_tip.on: How wide the drawing on screen may be before customer labels stop being drawn, measured across the window. Zoom out past this and no customer label is placed. Type 0 to leave customers unlabelled.

lpn_labels_restore_tip.on: Sets the label columns back to their original values: which properties are shown, the text before and after each one, the decimals, and the drop order. Your drawing and your other settings are not changed.

lpn_library_curve_copy.reply: There IS one button, and you are seeing the whole of it. js/looped-network.js:25580 is the Copy points button; :25710 is the TITLE of a window.prompt, which libCopyOut() reaches only when navigator.clipboard is missing or refused -- plain http, or an untrusted gesture. Your browser has the clipboard API, so you never see the prompt. Two strings, one button and one fallback.

lpn_library_curve_copy_tip.on: Copies every point as two columns, ready to paste into a spreadsheet.

lpn_library_curve_equation_tip.on: The curve fitted through the points, and the line drawn on the plot below. It is worked out from the points every time it is shown and is never stored, and its numbers are in the units the table above shows. The built-in solver runs on this equation; the EPANET engine reads the points themselves.

lpn_library_curve_in_use.on: This curve is used by {count} elements: {ids}. Point them at another curve first, then delete this one.

lpn_library_curve_note_tip.on: What this curve is, in your own words. It is written above the curve in an EPANET file and read back from there.

lpn_library_curve_values_tip.on: Select one or two columns in a spreadsheet, copy them, and paste into the first cell you want them to land in. The rows are added as they are needed. You can also paste lines copied straight out of an EPANET file, including the curve name.

lpn_library_fittings_in_use.on: This fittings list is used by {count} pipes: {ids}. Detach it from them before deleting it.

lpn_library_fittings_note.on: Each project has its own fittings library. A fittings list has fittings with a quantity for each one, and it adds up to a single minor loss coefficient. Both pipes and pipe types may refer to a list.

lpn_library_fittings_source.on: The fittings offered here are the thirteen in Table 3.3 of the EPANET 2.2 user manual. Choosing one copies its coefficient into the row, where you can change it. A coefficient depends on the size and the make of the fitting, so treat the table as a starting point rather than as an answer.

lpn_library_fittings_tip.on: A fittings list is a set of fittings and their quantities that several pipes can refer to. It adds up to one minor loss coefficient.

lpn_library_import_conflict.on: Skipped, because this project already has one of the same name: {names}. Nothing here was changed. Rename either one and import again if you want both.

lpn_library_import_curve_shape.on: These curves came across exactly as the file wrote them, and a run cannot use one until its first column rises from each point to the next: {names}
lpn_library_import_curve_shape.answer: Can you clarify "first column rises from each point to the next"?

lpn_library_import_needs_fittings.on: These pipe types refer to a fittings list this project does not have: {names}. Import the fittings library from the same file and they will find it.

lpn_library_import_no_libraries.on: That project file has no libraries to copy.

lpn_library_import_none.on: That project file has none of these to copy.

lpn_library_import_note.on: Each library you check is copied in whole. Delete what you do not want afterwards, the way you delete any other entry.

lpn_library_import_tip.on: Choose another project file and copy whole libraries from it into this project. Anything whose name is already taken here is skipped and listed, so nothing you already have is changed.

lpn_library_import_units.on: Warning: Units mismatch. Will be imported as is. Not recommended.

lpn_library_import_units_line.on: {name}: this project shows {mine}, the file shows {theirs}.

lpn_library_pipetype_blank_tip.on: Blank properties in a pipe type definition are left to be entered individually for each pipe.

lpn_library_pipetype_in_use.on: This pipe type is used by {count} pipes: {ids}. Detach it from them before deleting it.

lpn_library_pipetypes_note.on: Each project has its own pipe type library. You may leave properties blank in a pipe type definition. For example, a pipe type that specifies a roughness and no diameter is okay. You attach pipe types to pipes in their properties editor. Editing a definition here changes every pipe that references it.
lpn_library_pipetypes_note.answer: Please note the drastically different style here than what you have been using.

lpn_library_pipetypes_tip.on: A pipe type is a definition several pipes can refer to for their diameter, roughness and reaction coefficients. Editing the definition edits every pipe that uses it.

lpn_library_rule_bad.on: ⚠ This rule could not be read

lpn_library_rule_tip.on: One rule, in the words EPANET uses, one clause per line. A first line names it: RULE 1. Then a condition: IF TANK 2 LEVEL BELOW 17.1. Then what to do about it: THEN PUMP 9 STATUS IS OPEN. A last line may rank it: PRIORITY 1. Add AND or OR lines to test more than one thing, and ELSE lines to say what to do when the test fails. A condition can read LEVEL, HEAD, GRADE, PRESSURE or DEMAND on a node, FLOW, STATUS or SETTING on a link, or TIME and CLOCKTIME on SYSTEM. Write the numbers in the units this project is showing; they are converted for you. Leave the keywords in English; they are what the page and EPANET read.

lpn_library_rules_tip.on: A rule is a short paragraph that opens or closes a link, or gives it a setting, when a water level, a pressure, a flow or a time reaches a value you set. Rules can test more than one thing at once, and they can say what to do when the test fails.

lpn_lock_age_inuse.on: It has been in use for {x}.

lpn_lock_age_never_saved.on: Nothing has been saved to this file yet.

lpn_lock_age_unknown.on: There is no record of how long it has been in use, or when it was last saved or edited.

lpn_lock_ask_failed.on: Your message could not be delivered. Either nobody has this file open now, or the server could not be reached.

lpn_lock_ask_prompt.on: Who should we say is asking? Your initials are ideal. They are sent to whoever has the file open, and are stored only in this browser.

lpn_lock_ask_sent.on: We have asked whoever has this file open to close it. They will see it within a minute, if their page is still open. Nothing else has changed, and the file is still theirs until they close it.

lpn_lock_open_cancelled.on: That file was not opened, and nothing here changed. Somebody else still has it open.

lpn_lock_open_care.on: To avoid data loss, choose carefully from the options below.

lpn_lock_open_choices_ask.on: "Ask" tells whoever has this file open that you would like it, and changes nothing else. "Open read-only" lets you look at it and change anything you like, without being able to save here. "Break lock" lets you save over the file; their unsaved work is not lost, but they will no longer be able to save it here, and somebody may have to merge the two by hand.

lpn_lock_open_inuse.on: This file appears to be in use.

lpn_lock_requested.on: {name} would like to edit this file. When you are ready, save your work and use File, Close project to hand it over.

lpn_map_attach_done.on: The world map is behind your drawing now, and your project is unchanged. Use Map, World map, Detach to take it away again.

lpn_map_attach_none.on: There is no world map attached to this project yet. Use Map, World map, Attach first.

lpn_map_attach_readjust_tip.on: Return to Step 2 of the map attachment process.

lpn_map_attach_remove_tip.on: Take the world map away. The drawing and its coordinates are untouched either way.

lpn_map_attach_removed.on: The world map is gone, and the drawing is exactly as it was.

lpn_map_attach_scale_from_bad.on: Type a single number greater than zero.

lpn_map_attach_scale_from_done.on: The map is resized, and your drawing and every coordinate in it are exactly as they were.

lpn_map_attach_scale_from_prompt.on: Scale the map from its current size, about the middle of your drawing. 1 keeps it the same, 1.1 makes it 10% bigger, 0.9 makes it 10% smaller.

lpn_map_attach_tip.on: Attach the world map to this project without changing it any other way.

lpn_map_attach_turn.on: Map rotation in degrees, counterclockwise, where 0 puts north toward the top of the map
lpn_map_attach_turn.answer: Edited. Changed meaning. Please review carefully.

lpn_map_attach_where.on: Latitude and longitude of the middle of your drawing, in that order, separated by a comma or a space

lpn_map_unmeasurable.on: This page could not work out the size of the drawing area, so the map is showing the last view it was able to compute. Resizing the window makes it try again. If it keeps happening, a browser extension that blocks page measurements is the usual cause.

lpn_mapgeo_cancelled.on: The world map is back where it was, and your drawing never moved.

lpn_mapgeo_dial_help.on: Slide the two bars, or type in the boxes above them, to make the map bigger or smaller and to rotate it. The middle of each bar is the fit step 1 left, so 1 and 0 mean leave it alone. Arrow keys work on both.

lpn_mapgeo_gestures.on: Zoom moves your drawing and the map together, so you can see how well they line up. Dragging moves the map only.

lpn_mapgeo_hint1.on: Pan and zoom the map behind your drawing, or search for a place, or type a latitude and longitude. Then press Place approximately.

lpn_mapgeo_hint2.on: Drag anywhere to slide the map under your drawing. Your drawing and every coordinate in it stay exactly where they are. Press Georeference here when the map is right.

lpn_mapgeo_intro.on: Your drawing is on a map of the whole world, in the ocean at zero latitude and zero longitude. Find your own place first: pan and zoom the map behind the drawing, search for a place name, or type a latitude and longitude. The drawing itself does not move.

lpn_mapgeo_locked.on: Finish with the Georeference here button, or press Cancel, before you switch projects or save. The world map is still being placed.

lpn_mapgeo_readjust_intro.on: Your drawing is where you last placed it. To move it somewhere else, pan and zoom the map behind the drawing, search for a place name, or type a latitude and longitude. The drawing itself does not move.

lpn_mapgeo_replace.on: This project already has the world map attached. Replace that georeferencing?

lpn_mapgeo_step1.on: Step 1 of 2: find your place in the world

lpn_mapgeo_step2.on: Step 2 of 2: fit the map behind your drawing

lpn_menu_cue.on: Start with the menus above. Use the toolbar for quick access.

lpn_meter_pattern_unknown.on: No pattern in this project is named {id}, so the customer was left as it was.

lpn_meter_pick_pipe.on: Now click the pipe or the node that serves this customer. The customer stays where you put it. Press Escape to cancel.

lpn_meter_pipe_unknown.on: Nothing in this project is named {id}, so the customer was left where it was.

lpn_meter_placed.on: Customer {id} added. Its description and demand are typed in the Customers table, or press it in Select to open its box.

lpn_mixing_fraction_tip.on: The share of the tank volume that the inlet zone takes up, between 0 and 1. Only two compartment mixing uses it. Leave it empty and the whole tank is the inlet zone, which is what EPANET assumes.

lpn_mixing_model_tip.on: How the water already in this tank mixes with the water coming in. Complete mixing stirs the whole tank at once. Two-compartment mixing fills an inlet zone first and passes the rest on. FIFO plug flow moves the water through in the order it arrived. LIFO plug flow stacks it, so the last water in is the first water out. The choice changes the water age and the residual, and it does not change any pressure or flow.

lpn_mode_add_meter.on: Customer: click where the customer is, then click the pipe or the node that serves it. Or use Esc to cancel.

lpn_msglog_note.on: Newest first. This page keeps the last {n} messages while it is open, and nothing is stored on your computer.

lpn_msglog_tip.on: Read the recent messages again. They are kept only while this page is open.

lpn_multi_no_fields.on: These have nothing that can be set together here.

lpn_net_emergency.on: This was an EPANET .net file. That is EPANET's own project file, it has no published description, and this page reads it by working the format out from example files, so use it only when you have nothing else rather than as a dependable route. The .inp file is the documented format that every other program reads: in EPANET use File, Export, Network to write one, and import that instead whenever you can.

lpn_new_coordsys_local_tip.on: Not georeferenced. Attach your own background image or none.

lpn_new_coordsys_tip.on: Select the coordinate system of your network. This is permanent; the only way you can convert a network to different coordinates is with “File, Open to new coordinates”, and it is approximate.

lpn_new_units_tip.on: A project keeps its own units, so this choice belongs to this project alone and nothing here is saved as a browser setting. To start new projects a particular way, save an empty project as your template and make a copy of it each time.

lpn_node_customers_tip.on: List of customers added at this node (because this was nearest). Customer demands are in addition to other demands listed here. A customer is edited where it sits on the map or in the Customers table.

lpn_pane_filter_none.on: Nothing in this table matches the filter.

lpn_pipetype_detach_tip.on: Copies the values this pipe reads from its type into the pipe itself and stops using the type. The pipe’s values don’t change now, and from now on you can edit these values here.

lpn_profile_delete_confirm.on: Delete the saved path {name}? The drawing itself is not changed.

lpn_profile_edit_click.on: Drag any point on the path to move it. Click a point you added to take it off.

lpn_profile_edit_nowhere.on: A point on the path has to be a node. The path is unchanged.

lpn_profile_edit_tap.on: Drag any point on the path to move it. Tap a point you added to take it off.

lpn_profile_edit_tip.on: Change one end of the path, or take one node off it, without drawing the whole path again.

lpn_profile_missing.on: {name} names nodes that are not in this project: {ids}

lpn_pump_curve_source_tip.on: The curve in the Libraries box that says how much head this pump adds at each flow. Several pumps can use the same curve, and editing it there changes all of them. This pump holds only the reference; the points themselves are read and edited under Libraries, Curves.

lpn_pump_effic_curve_tip.on: The curve in the Libraries box that says how efficient this pump is at each flow. Several pumps can use the same curve, and editing it there changes all of them. This pump holds only the reference; the points themselves are read and edited under Libraries, Curves.

lpn_pump_effic_global.on: This pump has no efficiency curve selected, so it runs at the efficiency set for the whole network, {percent}.

lpn_pump_effic_note.on: Flow vs percent efficiency. A pump with no efficiency curve selected runs at the network efficiency.

lpn_pump_effic_unstated.on: This pump refers to an efficiency curve called {name}, which nothing in this project defines, so it runs at the efficiency set for the whole network, {percent}.

lpn_quality_chemical.on: A chemical this file names (kept, not worked out)

lpn_quality_chemical_name_tip.on: The name of the chemical and the units its concentrations are written in: for example, write Chlorine mg/L as one entry. This is a label. EPANET does not convert a concentration, so every concentration and every coefficient in the project has to be written in these units already.

lpn_quality_initial_tip.on: How much of the chemical this node holds when the run starts. A reservoir holds its own value for the whole run, which is how the residual leaving a treatment plant is usually stated. Leave it empty and the node starts with none of the chemical.

lpn_quality_needs_run.on: Water quality is carried along the pipes over time, so it needs the EPANET engine and a total run time. Set a Total run time under Time, then press Run.

lpn_reaction_bulk_tip.on: Reaction in the body of the water, used for every pipe that does not carry its own. A negative number decays the chemical and a positive one increases it. The reaction is first order unless an imported EPANET file states another order, so the coefficient is a rate in 1/day. An empty box means no bulk reaction.

lpn_reaction_note.on: This page offers no reaction coefficient of its own. There is no standard test for one, and published field values for the same kind of water differ by a factor of ten, so a number supplied here would be read as a recommendation. Enter one you have measured or one you can cite, or leave the boxes empty for a chemical that does not react.

lpn_reaction_pipe_tip.on: This pipe on its own. Leave it empty and the pipe uses the coefficient set for the whole network under Settings, Water quality.

lpn_reaction_tank_tip.on: Reaction in the water held in this tank, as a rate in 1/day. A negative number decays the chemical and a positive one grows it. Water stands in a tank far longer than it stands in any pipe, so this is often where a residual is lost. Leave it empty and the tank uses the bulk reaction coefficient set for the whole network under Settings, Water quality.

lpn_reaction_wall_tip.on: Reaction at the pipe wall, used for every pipe that does not carry its own. A negative number decays the chemical. The reaction is first order unless an imported EPANET file states another order, so the coefficient is a length per day, written in the project length unit. An empty box means no wall reaction.

lpn_replace_asked.on: Asked for {n}. The answer is on its way.

lpn_replace_q_bad.on: This query cannot be read, so there is nothing to change. Fix it above first.

lpn_reports_menu_tip.on: The finished answers this page produces once a network has been calculated: what the pumps cost, how the scenarios compare, and what the EPANET solver itself printed.

lpn_result_concentration_tip.on: How much of the chemical is left at this point after it has travelled and reacted. The units are the ones named beside the chemical under Settings, Water quality.

lpn_result_demand_tip.on: The flow this node draws at the time step shown: the total of base demands multiplied by their patterns. Worked out, not typed, so it changes with the clock and cannot be edited.

lpn_result_source_share_tip.on: The source trace share reports how much of the water reaching this point came from the trace node.

lpn_result_water_age_tip.on: How long the water reaching this point has been in the system. There is no standard number to compare it against, so read it as a measurement and judge it yourself.

lpn_rule_dangling_note.on: These rules refer to an element that is no longer in this project, so they were ignored in this run: {ids}

lpn_rule_unreadable_note.on: These rules could not be read, so they were ignored in this run: {ids}

lpn_scenario_mark_tip.on: Ringed: this element holds a value that belongs to the scenario {name} alone.

lpn_scenario_overrides.reply: You are right and the finding was wrong: 'No. of custom values' is yours, set 2026-09-04 in commit fdde7943, and Wave 0 re-read it cold two days later. Fixed at the source rather than noted -- wave0_keyset.php now drops every key whose exact current English carries a ruling, which took 146 keys out of the next pass. On the $ec_lang_syn you remember giving: it is in no commit and not in the working tree, so it never reached a file. Paste it again and it goes in.

lpn_scenario_overrides_tip.on: Each of those values is marked on the map with an amber ring. Switch to Base to see the drawing without them.

lpn_scncmp_empty.on: Nothing has been drawn yet, so there is nothing to solve.

lpn_scncmp_menu_tip.on: Solve every scenario in this project and read them side by side: the lowest pressure and the highest velocity in each.

lpn_scncmp_note.on: Every scenario is solved from a copy of the drawing. Nothing here changes the project, and the scenario you are working in is left as it was.

lpn_setbox_divider.on: Width of the Settings section list

lpn_settings_accuracy_tip.on: How close the solver has to get before it stops, measured as the flow still changing from one trial to the next. A smaller number is more exact and takes longer. Both solvers read this one box, and each measures that change against a different total: the built-in solver against the sum of the demands, EPANET against the sum of the link flows. Left empty, this page tries far harder than EPANET does on its own.

lpn_settings_area_hint_tip.on: Shows the bubble over the map that says what your next click will do while you are selecting an area.

lpn_settings_custom_props_note.on: Properties you define yourself for your own purposes. They are stored with the project and scenarios like all other properties.

lpn_settings_damp_limit_tip.on: The accuracy at which the solver begins taking smaller steps, which can help a network that is swinging back and forth to converge. Zero means it never does. Only the EPANET solver reads this box.

lpn_settings_demand_multiplier_tip.on: One scale on every demand in the network at once. Use it to ask what the system does at more or less than today's use. It does not change the numbers you typed.

lpn_settings_elev_source_tip.on: Where a new node gets its elevation. The land surface is read from Mapbox DEM, which is about 30 m across on most of the Earth and finer where better data exists.

lpn_settings_emitter_exponent_tip.on: The power in the sprinkler and leak law, flow = coefficient x pressure to this power. It only changes the answer where a node has an emitter, which for now means a network read from an EPANET file.

lpn_settings_flow_change_tip.on: An additional test the solver must pass before it stops: the maximum change in any one pipe's flow from one trial to the next. Zero means do not apply this test. Only the EPANET solver reads this box.

lpn_settings_head_error_tip.on: An additional test the solver must pass before it stops: the largest head any one pipe is still out by. Zero means do not apply this test. Only the EPANET solver reads this box.

lpn_settings_label_max_width.on: Show labels when zoomed to this map width or less

lpn_settings_label_max_width_tip.on: Labels are drawn only while the map is this wide or narrower. Leave the box blank to draw them at every zoom.

lpn_settings_leader_snap_tip.on: When you drag a label away from what it names, the line back to it is pulled onto the nearest round angle if you drag close to one. Keep dragging and it lets go, so any angle is still available. Off drags freely, which is what this page has always done.

lpn_settings_quality_source_tip.on: The point whose water is traced. Every other point then shows the share of its water that came from here.

lpn_settings_quality_track_tip.on: Choose what the run should follow through the pipes: how long the water has been in the system, or where it came from. Neither one asks you for any other number.

lpn_settings_runbox_tip.on: A box that reports how far a run has got and what it found. With it turned off, a finished run says the same thing in the status line for a few seconds instead. This is a setting for this browser, not for the project.

lpn_settings_show_arrows_tip.on: Draw an arrow on each pipe showing which way the water is running. The arrows appear after a run, and turning them off leaves the results unchanged. This setting is saved with the project.

lpn_settings_specific_gravity_tip.on: The weight of the fluid compared with water. It changes the pressures a gauge would read, not the flows.

lpn_settings_symbol_cap.on: Prevent nodes from scaling larger than

lpn_settings_symbol_cap_tip.on: A junction stops growing on the ground once its diameter would be this many times the length of the pipe at this percentile of all pipe lengths in the network. Past that point on the map, junctions, pipes and other symbols shrink on the screen as you zoom out instead of growing on the ground. Reservoirs and tanks are the exception and keep their screen size at every zoom.

lpn_settings_trials_tip.on: How many trials are allowed before the solver gives up on a network that will not converge.

lpn_settings_unbalanced_tip.on: What to do with a network that has used up its trials and still has not converged. Keeping on allows the extra trials below, which often reaches convergence; stopping reports the last trial as it stands, which is close but not a solution. Only the EPANET solver reads this box. The built-in solver always stops and marks the answer as not converged.

lpn_settings_unbalanced_trials_tip.on: How many further trials to allow after the maximum above is used up, before the last trial is reported. Only the EPANET solver reads this box.

lpn_settings_viscosity_tip.on: The viscosity of the fluid compared with water at 20 degrees Celsius. It only changes the answer under the Darcy-Weisbach method.

lpn_source_pattern_tip.on: A time pattern that scales the dose through the run, for a feed that is not constant. No pattern means that the dose is the same at every step.

lpn_source_quality_tip.on: How strong the dose is. For every type but the mass booster this is a concentration, in the units named beside the chemical under Settings, Water quality; for a mass booster it is a mass of chemical per minute. Leave it empty and nothing is added here, which is not the same as a zero: a zero is a feed that is running and adding nothing.

lpn_source_type_tip.on: What kind of dose this node applies to the water passing through it. Concentration treats the water entering the network here as arriving at the Source quality value. Mass booster adds a mass of chemical every minute, whatever the flow is. Setpoint booster lifts the concentration leaving this node to the Source quality value and no further. Flow-paced booster adds the Source quality value to whatever is already in the water.

lpn_storage_unreadable.on: Not saved. This project could not be read from browser storage. Its stored copy is left exactly as it is and will not be written over, so nothing on this tab is being saved. Open a file or create a new project to keep working.

lpn_survey_cancelled.on: Nothing was created and nothing was changed.

lpn_survey_confirm.on: Create {n} junction(s) from this surveyed point list?

lpn_survey_confirm_pipes.on: No pipes are drawn. A surveyed list says where the points are, not which of them are joined.

lpn_survey_elev_assumed.on: The file does not say what unit its elevations are in, so they are read as {project}, which is the unit this project is showing.

lpn_survey_elev_unit.on: Elevations in the file are read as {file}, and this project is showing {project}.
lpn_survey_elev_unit.answer: Under what condition would we know the units of the file?

lpn_survey_err_ambiguous_coord.on: More than one column in that file could be the {axis} ({detail}), and this page will not choose between them. Leave one of them named as the {axis} and try again.

lpn_survey_err_ambiguous_lon.on: More than one column in that file could be the longitude ({detail}), and this page will not choose between them. Leave one of them named as the longitude and try again.
lpn_survey_err_ambiguous_lon.answer: Needs discussion and design concept planning.

lpn_survey_err_empty.on: That file has nothing in it.

lpn_survey_err_gpx_no_wpt.on: That GPX file holds no waypoints, so there is nothing to make junctions from.

lpn_survey_err_no_coords.on: Could not find two coordinate columns in that file. Name two of the columns in the first row of the file, and try again. The first row reads: {detail}

lpn_survey_err_no_points.on: Not one row of that file could be read as a surveyed point. Rows read: {detail}

lpn_survey_err_plane.on: That file holds plane survey coordinates ({detail}), not latitude and longitude. A northing is a distance across a flat plane, and this page cannot yet turn one into a position on the Earth, so nothing was read. Export the same points as latitude and longitude, in decimal degrees, and try again.
lpn_survey_err_plane.answer: Needs discussion and design concept planning.

lpn_survey_err_unreadable.on: That file could not be read as a surveyed point list.

lpn_survey_fmt_enz.on: Easting, northing, elevation (ENZ, also written XYZ)

lpn_survey_map_gpx.on: Each waypoint becomes one junction, at its own latitude and longitude, taking the name and the elevation the file states for it. A GPX elevation is in meters by definition of the format.

lpn_survey_map_lines.on: Latitude comes from the column {lat}, longitude from {lon}, the name from {id}, and the elevation from {elev}.

lpn_survey_not_geo.on: A surveyed point list is latitude and longitude, and this project is not on a map of the Earth. Start a geographic project from File, New, and import the list into that one.
lpn_survey_not_geo.answer: Needs discussion and design concept planning.

lpn_survey_note_ambiguous_elev.on: More than one column could be the elevation, so none of them was read.

lpn_survey_note_bad_coord.on: The {axis} does not read as a number.

lpn_survey_note_bad_lon.on: The longitude here does not read as a decimal number of degrees ({detail}), so no junction was made for this row. Degrees, minutes and seconds are not read; convert them to decimal degrees first.
lpn_survey_note_bad_lon.answer: Needs discussion and design concept planning.

lpn_survey_note_coord_range.on: The {axis} is outside the range this project allows.

lpn_survey_note_elev_converted.on: The elevation column in your file is named for {detail}, which is not the unit this project is showing, so those numbers were converted. Every other number came across exactly as the file states it.

lpn_survey_note_gpx_rtept.on: The file also holds {detail} route point(s), which were not made into junctions.

lpn_survey_note_gpx_trkpt.on: The file also holds {detail} track point(s). Those are a record of where somebody walked rather than places they surveyed, so they were not made into junctions.

lpn_survey_note_header_unread.on: The first line was skipped: it names no columns this page knows.

lpn_survey_note_id_duplicate.on: Name already used earlier in this file, new name assigned.

lpn_survey_note_id_invalid.on: Name cannot be used here, new name assigned.

lpn_survey_note_id_taken.on: Name already in project, new name assigned.

lpn_survey_note_lon_missing.on: The longitude column is empty on this row, so no junction was made for it.
lpn_survey_note_lon_missing.answer: Needs discussion and design concept planning.

lpn_survey_note_lon_range.on: This longitude is outside the range a longitude can have ({detail}), so no junction was made for this row.

lpn_survey_note_row_short.on: Too few columns for the file format above.

lpn_survey_read_error.on: That file could not be read from your disk.

lpn_survey_report_clean.on: Every point in the file came across, and nothing was changed on the way in.

lpn_survey_report_elev.on: {n} of them took an elevation from the file.

lpn_survey_report_lead.on: Nothing in your file was thrown away quietly. Below is every row that could not be taken as it stands, and everything that was changed on the way in:

lpn_terrain_denied.on: The terrain service refused the request ({status}), so no elevation was changed. The Mapbox token this site uses may not allow the web address you are on.

lpn_terrain_http.on: The terrain service answered with an error ({status}), so no elevation was changed. Nothing is wrong with your network.

lpn_terrain_no_place.on: None of those nodes has a position on the Earth, so nothing was sent and no elevation was changed. Reading the land surface needs a project in latitude and longitude, or one on a projection this page can place.

lpn_terrain_rate_limited.on: The terrain service is asking us to slow down (429), so no elevation was changed. Try again in a minute.

lpn_terrain_will_ids.on: These are the nodes that will be filled in: {ids}

lpn_time_runbox_hide.on: Do not show this box again

lpn_tool_add_meter_tip.on: Click where the customer is, then click the pipe or the node that serves it. The demand you give the customer is added to the junction at the near end of that pipe.

lpn_tool_area_tip.on: Click on the map as instructed to select everything inside the shape. Press this button again to change the shape between a window, a lasso and a polygon. Hold Shift while selecting to continue with the existing selection, adding or removing (toggle) what you select.

lpn_ts_add_none.on: Nothing of that kind is chosen on the map.

lpn_ts_add_tip.on: Put everything now chosen on the map onto the graph.

lpn_ts_group_tip.on: Whether the graph shows nodes or links.

lpn_ts_no_frames.on: No extended period results yet. Press Calculate to run the simulation.

lpn_ts_none.on: Nothing to graph yet. Choose assets on the map and press Add selected.

lpn_ts_quantity_tip.on: Which value to graph against time.

lpn_ts_tip.on: Graph one or more assets against time across an extended period simulation.

lpn_wrong_tip.on: One press tells us that something on this page is wrong. It sends the name of this page, the language you are reading it in, and the message on the map if there is one. It sends nothing you have typed, no address, and nothing at all out of your drawing. Nobody can write back, because this tells us nothing about who you are. Use Help, Fix something when you want to say more.
